sentences.text: The petitioner as complainant had filed a complaint under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. in Crl.M.P.No.138 of 2024 before the Lower Court seeking direction directing the 1st respondent to register an FIR under Sections 406, 498, 506(ii) IPC.
The Trial Court by order dated 16.08.2024, dismissed the same.
Against which the present revision has been filed.

2. The contention of the petitioner is that the marriage between the petitioner and 2nd respondent,
Jeyaseelan solemnized on 15.05.2013 and after the marriage she had been residing with her husband and in-laws at No.2, PDMS Sanjeevi Gandhi Nagar, Ulaipallar Nagar, 9th Street,
Pattabiram.

At the time of the marriage, the parents of the petitioner gave 15 sovereigns of gold jewels to her and 4 sovereigns of gold jewels to her husband, the 2nd respondent including all Sreedhana articles.
A Pulsar Bike was also given to the 2nd respondent.
All the Marriage expenses were borne by the petitioners parents.

3. After the marriage, the 2nd respondent and his family members https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis started demanding dowry and under various pretexts, the petitioner was harassed, beaten and subjected to cruelty.
The petitioner's father-in-law also attempted to misbehave with her.

Therefore,
a complaint was lodged by the petitioner.

However, after the intervention of the elders of the family,
the matter was compromised between the parties.

Further, the harassment and demand for dowry continued and without informing the petitioner, the 2nd respondent had left abroad for employment and was unable to be contacted and again a complaint was made.
This time also the matter was compromised between the parties and they agreed to a reunion.
4. On 17.07.2023, while the petitioner was at her in-laws place at Pattabiram, the accused 2 to 4 herein initiated a quarrel, using filthy language against her and demanding dowry.
They also physically assaulted her with a broomstick and with hands, even attempted to kill her by trampling on her neck.
As a result, she sustained injuries.
Thereafter, the petitioners father admitted her at Kilpauk, Medical College, Hospital.
While she was in the hospital, her husband and in-laws came to the hospital and again threatened her.

Hence, she lodged a complaint to the Inspector of Police,
W-4, All Women Police Station, Kilpauk.
Since no action was taken, she sent a representation to the Deputy Commissioner of Police.
Thereafter too no https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis action was taken on her representation.
Hence, she filed a petition under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C to direct the respondent police to register an FIR before the Additional Mahila Court, Egmore, Chennai.
However, the Trial Court had dismissed the petition, against which the present revision filed.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the Apex Court had time and again held that for the offence under Section 498A IPC, the jurisdiction of the victim wherever she presently resides can be invoked and it is not necessary that the place of occurrence should be her in-law's place.
6.

The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that prior to lodging a complaint before the 1st respondent police, for the very same occurrence, the petitioner had lodged a complaint before the All Women Police, Pattabiram on 17.07.2023 for which CSR.No.55/2023 was assigned.

Thereafter,
the petitioner was called for inquiry.
However, the petitioner had failed to attend the enquiry and the enquiry in CSR.No.55/2023 is still pending.

7. The learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the 1st respondent police fairly submitted that if the petitioner appears with the relevant https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis documents before the Inspector of Police, W-37, All Women Police Station, Pattabiram, after verification and recording of the statement, if an offence is made out, appropriate steps would be taken on the complaint and investigation would be conducted.
The petitioner's apprehension that the Pattabiram Police are not taking immediate and effective steps is unwarranted.
Appropriate instruction will be given to the Pattabiram Police.

8. Considering the submissions and the fact that the petitioner had already lodged a complaint with the Pattabiram Police and CSR No.55/2023 was assigned for the occurrence on 17.07.2023, the Inspector of Police, W.37, All Women Police Station, Pattabiram is directed to conduct enquiry and thereafter register an FIR if cognizable offence made out and further proceed with the case in accordance with law.
It is made clear that the sufferings and the cruelty inflicted upon the victim cannot lost be sight of.
The averments contained in the complaint disclose offence under Section 498 A IPC.
The Inspector of Police, W.37, All Women Police Station.
Pattabiram is directed to act accordingly.
